notes: Baseline (without_skill) rows are copied from iteration-1 (1 run per eval); with_skill is 3 runs for evals 0-2 and 1 run for the new evals 3-4. The header's '3 runs each' is the aggregator's default wording.

Like-for-like on evals 0-2, with_skill went from 143.0s / 66.4k tokens (iteration-1) to 90.1s / 54.2k tokens: -37% time, -18% tokens, pass rate unchanged at 100%. Per eval: eval-0 181->123s, eval-1 112->83s, eval-2 137->65s.

eval-2 (small scaffold) flipped from slower than baseline (137s vs 102s) to faster (65s), and now uses about as many tokens (44k vs 43k). The script's grouped stub finding replaced the agent's page-by-page stub audit.

Token floor is ~40k: the structure-only run (eval-4) used 39.6k tokens with 4 tool calls, so most of the remaining cost is loading context, not doing the work. The <=50k target is met only by evals 2 and 4; eval-0 (a real repo with code spot-checks) stays around 61k.
The structure-only fast path works: eval-4 finished in 23.8s with a 27-line report and explicitly skipped the qualitative pass.
Reports shrank and stopped listing checks that passed: 25-37 lines in iteration-2 against 60-138 in iteration-1, with no assertion lost.

Qualitative additions survived the budget: runs still found the 'make check' target missing, reading-map promises without pages, placeholder github.com/example links (eval-1), and confirmed the generated pages are current by running their freshness test (eval-0).
eval-3 found a script false positive (the docs index was read from above --repo-root). It is fixed after the run; the fix changes only that warning.

Harness note: subagent Write of report files was blocked in 3 runs. Two runs returned the text and the orchestrator saved it, which slightly understates their time. One run wrote the file with a shell heredoc instead.
